precepts.point: The so-called Jews boast of the temple and their heritage in a land that does not belong to them, but the man who built the first temple was a black man, and the scripture says so plainly.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

precepts.why:
“I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.” Solomon by his own word is black.

So when Solomon “had finished the building of the house of the Lord”, and the Most High appeared to him the second time as at Gibeon, the man who built the first temple was a black man, and the scripture says so plainly. The so-called Jews boast of the temple and their heritage in a land that does not belong to them, but the builder of that temple was black.

precepts.point: The bride longs for the king's love, calling it better than wine; the savor of his good ointments makes his name as ointment poured forth, and therefore the virgins love him. Drawn into the king's chambers, they are glad and rejoice in him.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

precepts.why:
“The song of songs, which is Solomon’s.” Solomon is the author, not a woman, though that is the doctrine some try to push. The plain words say these songs belong to Solomon, and the history shows why. “And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore.”

His wisdom “excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt. For he was wiser than all men”, wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Chalcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol, “and his fame was in all nations round about.”

“And he spake three thousand proverbs: and his songs were a thousand and five.” Solomon was a poet, and his thousand and five songs mark him plainly as the writer of this book.

precepts.text: Seek out of the book of the Most High and read, for the scriptures confirm one another and none fails.
precepts.point: The bride longs for the king's love, calling it better than wine; the savor of his good ointments makes his name as ointment poured forth, and therefore the virgins love him. Drawn into the king's chambers, they are glad and rejoice in him.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

precepts.why:
“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate: for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.”

The scriptures confirm one another and none fails. So the question of who wrote the song of songs is not settled by doctrine pushed from outside; it is settled by seeking out of the book and reading, where verse one and the record of Solomon's thousand and five songs are mates.

points: The bride says, "I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem," likening herself to the tents of Kedar and the curtains of Solomon.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

points: She says, look not upon me because I am black, because the sun has looked upon me; her mother's children were angry with her and made her keeper of the vineyards, but her own vineyard she has not kept.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

points: She asks the one her soul loves where he feeds his flock and where he makes it rest at noon, so she need not wander as one who turns aside by the flocks of his companions.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

points: The answer: if she does not know, then O fairest among women, go by the footsteps of the flock and feed her kids beside the shepherds' tents.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

points: He compares his love to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots, and praises her cheeks comely with rows of jewels and her neck with chains of gold.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

points: They will make her borders of gold with studs of silver.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

points: While the king sits at his table, her spikenard sends forth its smell; her wellbeloved is a bundle of myrrh that shall lie all night between her breasts, and a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

points: He tells her, behold you are fair, my love, you have doves' eyes; and she answers that he is fair and pleasant, and their bed is green.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

points: The beams of their house are cedar and their rafters of fir.

note.label: Song of Solomon 1: The Song of Songs, Which Is Solomon's

points: “I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem”. Solomon is black and good-looking, black and handsome. Correlate blackness with being good-looking. God said it. To hell with what this world says. Believe and teach it. Sisters have trouble complimenting another sister, saying she looks cute. Why? Encourage each other. Brothers, don't go telling another brother he's cute or handsome like that.
He's saying it to the daughters of Jerusalem because our sisters battle with self-esteem. Be okay with your blackness; love it. Sisters, work on your self-esteem.
